sentences.text: Hon'ble Mr. Justice Rongon Mukhopadhyay Hon'ble Mr. Justice Deepak Roshan

--- 
 For the Appellant : Mr. Vikas Kumar, Adv.
For the State : Mr. Abhay Kr. Tiwari, A.P.P.

I.A. No. 5486 of 2024 7/13.06.2024 Heard Mr. Vikas Kumar, learned counsel for the appellant and  Mr. Abhay Kumar Tiwari, learned A.P.P.
This application has been preferred by the appellant for grant of bail during pendency of this appeal.

The appellant has been convicted for the offence punishable under Section 376(2)(n) and 376(3)
I.P.C. and Section 6 POCSO Act and has been sentenced to undergo imprisonment for life which shall mean imprisonment for the remainder of a person's natural life along with a fine of Rs.20,000/- for the offence punishable under Section 6 of the POCSO Act.
The allegation reveals that during Mangala Puja in the year 2019 the appellant came to house of his aunt and had taken away the victim towards the jungle and had made physical relationship with her.
The victim on account of such physical relationship had become pregnant and she had subsequently delivered a child.
It has been submitted by learned counsel for the appellant that the appellant is in custody since 9.9.2019.

It has also been submitted that there was a love affair between the appellant and the victim who has been examined as P.W.2 and her cross-examination also indicates that she was in love with the appellant.
Learned A.P.P. has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant.

The evidence of the victim 'X' who Karan Patar @ Karan Patra vs The State Of Jharkhand on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147941798/
1 has been examined as P.W.2 clearly revels that she was in love with the appellant and had made physical relationship with him.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It would thus appear that the appellant and the victim were in a love affair which resulted in a physical relationship between them and consequently a child was born to the victim.
The appellant has remained in custody for almost five years.

Regard being had to the aforesaid facts, the appellant during pendency of this appeal is directed to be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (rupees ten thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each, to the satisfaction of learned Special Judge, POCSO, Jamshedpur in connection with Spl. POCSO Case No.72 of 2019.

(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J.) (Deepak Roshan, J.) Shamim/
